subject: Re: Limited model-training rights — product+security input needed
messages:
From: Laura Chen <laura.chen@atlanticai.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: contracts@atlanticai.com
Date: Sun, 14 Feb 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Clarification on DPA — use of customer data for model training

Monica,

Thanks for sending over the draft DPA. Our legal team flagged Section 5.2 that allows Redwood to use customer-provided content to improve models. For Atlantic AI's regulatory posture we need a firm statement that our data will not be used to train or improve base model weights without explicit opt-in.

Can you confirm whether Redwood would agree to one of the following:
- a firm "no training" commitment (no use for model weights), or
- a scoped opt-in that requires a separate training addendum and explicit signatures?

We appreciate a quick yes/no and any suggested redline language so we can get this to our procurement this week.

Best,
Laura Chen
Head of Partnerships
Atlantic AI

Attachments: atlantic-dpa-redline.pdf (redline)

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: dev.patel@redwood.ai, irene.choi@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 14 Feb 2027 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Clarification on DPA — use of customer data for model training

Team — forwarding Atlantic's ask. They want an explicit "no training" commitment in the DPA (or an opt-in addendum). They're pushing to close the deal this week (DEAL-4312).

Quick context: the current DPA has general "use" language that legal drafted to allow service improvements; Atlantic's procurement wants that removed or scoped. They attached their redline (see attachment).

Asks:
- Product (Dev): what would it take operationally to guarantee no customer data touches any training pipeline or aggregate weight updates? If we can't do a guarantee, what mitigations can we offer (e.g., dedicated non-training inference-only variant, strict telemetry sampling rules, contractual auditability)?
- Security (Irene): what telemetry/metadata do we collect that might be considered training signal? Can we provide an attestation and operational controls (logs, retention, subprocessor list)?

I've attached a proposed training addendum template I grabbed from a previous customer. Please reply with recommended language and any timing constraints. I may respond to the customer directly once we have a draft.

Thanks — Monica
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0124

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: irene.choi@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 14 Feb 2027 13:27:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Clarification on DPA — use of customer data for model training

Monica — thanks for the flag. Short answers up front: we can operationally guarantee that customer request/response content is not used to update any shared base model weights, with caveats around telemetry and logging that I note below. Implementation options:

1) Contractual no-training commitment + technical enforcement
   - We can tag Atlantic's customer ID and block data pipelines that feed into training buckets. That requires a one-time config change and a test (1-2 business days).
2) Inference-only instance (Dedicated or Private)
   - If they need absolute isolation, a dedicated inference pool with disabled internal training hooks is simplest; more cost but stronger guarantee.
3) Telemetry audit and attestation
   - We can produce an attestation of pipeline separation and export logs for a defined retention window; security will need to confirm exact fields.

Caveats:
- Our telemetry may collect aggregated token stats and system traces for performance debugging. We can disable or redact token-level telemetry for this tenant, but we'll need a small config change and some testing.
- Subprocessor list: if any third-party analytics or observability vendors receive telemetry, that must be scoped in the DPA's subprocessor schedule.

Suggested redline language for a training addendum (draft):
"Redwood Inference will not, directly or indirectly, use Customer Content to train, improve, or update the weights of any of Redwood's base or foundation models without Customer's express, written opt-in. Redwood will segregate Customer Content from any training pipelines and, upon request, provide reasonable evidence of such segregation, subject to Redwoods' internal security practices and redaction of third-party confidential information."

If the customer wants formal proof, we can offer the dedicated inference option + quarterly attestation. I can craft a short, product-accurate paragraph for the addendum if we want to offer both contract + technical option.

Timeline: I can get a product-accurate addendum paragraph to you within 4 hours and a full operations checklist for security in 1 business day.

— Dev
Senior Product Manager, Inference
dev.patel@redwood.ai

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, dev.patel@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 15 Feb 2027 08:46:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Clarification on DPA — use of customer data for model training

Monica / Dev — this is straightforward but we should be precise. Security notes: 

- Telemetry: our default telemetry pipeline includes request IDs, request timestamps, service latency, error rates, and exception traces. We do NOT persist full customer prompt/response content in training datasets by default. However, there are internal debug flows where token-level traces may be retained for a short window (24-72 hours) for incident response. We can disable token-level traces for Atlantic and redact any logs within that window.
- Subprocessors: we must include the observability vendor (TelemetryCo) and our metrics provider (CloudMetrics) in the subprocessor schedule if any telemetry is retained outside RW systems.
- Attestation: we can provide "Operational Segregation Attestation" stating that Atlantic's tenant is excluded from training pipelines and listing the controls in place (config tags, pipeline filters, retention policy). That attestation will include non-sensitive logs and timestamps but will not expose internal system configs.

Proposed additional DPA clause: 
"Redwood will not use Customer Content to train Redwood models without Customer's prior written consent. Redwood will, upon Customer request, provide an Operational Segregation Attestation and cooperate with reasonable audits (redacted as necessary to protect Redwood's proprietary systems or third-party confidential information)."

I'll attach a short security FAQ that explains the telemetry fields and the operational steps we'll take to segregate data. For Atlantic, if they want the highest assurance, recommend Dedicated inference + the addendum. Otherwise, the contractual no-training clause + telemetry suppression + attestation should be acceptable.

— Irene Choi
Head of Security, Redwood Inference
irene.choi@redwood.ai

Attachments: security-faq.pdf

1) Contractual no-training addendum (no-cost)
   - Contract language: "Redwood Inference will not, directly or indirectly, use Customer Content to train, improve, or update the weights of any Redwood base or foundation models without Customer's express, written opt-in. Redwood will segregate Customer Content from training pipelines and provide an Operational Segregation Attestation upon request."
   - Operational steps: disable token-level telemetry for Atlantic's tenant and tag their tenant id to exclude from training buckets. Security will provide an attestation within 5 business days of request.

2) Dedicated inference pool (recommended for highest assurance; cost applies)
   - Fully isolated inference capacity with training hooks disabled. Quarterly attestation and optional third-party audit (scope and cost TBD).

Attached is a clean addendum paragraph and a redline of your DPA showing the suggested edits. If option 1 works, I can get a DocuSign envelope started today (link below). If they need dedicated, we can get procurement pricing in parallel.

Proposed next step: let me know whether Atlantic prefers (1) or (2) by EOD; I'll route the appropriate paperwork.
